title: A request that never completes logs nothing: no request-start event
description:
`crates/mimid-server/src/http.rs` turns the trace layer's request event
off (`.on_request(())`) and logs only on response, at `debug`:

    .on_response(|response, latency, span| { ... tracing::debug!(status, elapsed_ms, "request completed") })

So a request that never completes logs nothing at all. There is no line
saying the server took it, no line saying what it is waiting for, and
the response event cannot fire.

Mark 2026-11-27: "nothing ever should hang, lock up, or go silent when
sent something to process. ever. thats always a bug."

## What it blocks

Two waits could not be converted in the event sweep and still sleep on a
guess, each marked in the code with this bead's id:

- `crates/mimid-server/tests/binary_smoke.rs`, the shutdown grace-period
  test: sleeps 500 ms to let the server start a request that never
  finishes, because nothing says when it has.
- `crates/mimid-server/tests/mtls_binaries.rs`, `Jmap::next`: the
  providers are separate processes whose only observable is their JSON
  log, and storing a fanout logs nothing at the `info` level they run
  at.

It also blocks the operator's side of the same question, which is the
reason to do it rather than a test's convenience: a provider that has
gone quiet under load gives nobody a way to see which requests are in
flight.

## What to do

Emit an event when a request starts, inside the `http_request` span so
it carries the method and route already recorded there. `debug` is the
level for it: one line per request, off in production by default, on
when someone is looking.

Decide the target deliberately. The binary's own events are target
`mimid`, mimid-server's are `mimid_server`, and the tests' filters say
`mimid=info`, so a new event in `http.rs` needs `mimid_server=debug` to
appear. Whichever is chosen, the tests that wait on the line set that
filter.

Then also consider a `fanout accepted` event at `info` rather than
`debug` (`crates/mimid-server/src/follower/notify.rs`), which is what
`mtls_binaries` would follow: a delivery stored is a fact an operator
wants, and it is one line per fanout, not per message.
